source: Echterhoff et al. (2024) Cognitive Bias in Decision-Making with LLMs (BiasBuster)
finding: Built 13,465 prompts for cognitive biases (anchoring/sequential, framing, status quo, group attribution, primacy) in a student-admissions task. Tested awareness, contrastive, counterfactual and self-help prompts on four models.
numbers: Models: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, Llama-2 7B and 13B. GPT-4 admitted 40.5% more students under reject framing than admit framing. Llama-2 7B rated 32.1% fewer females as good at math. Options A/B were picked more often than C/D (primacy).
quote: Be mindful to prompting not be biased by cognitive bias.
limits: Zero-shot awareness gave only small gains. Few-shot (contrastive, counterfactual) sometimes made the model fail: admission rate went to nearly 0 or 1. Anchoring self-help worked only for large models; Llama changed 40-52% of decisions.
agent_relevance: A bare warning is weak and examples can break the output format. Worked examples need a format check. Rewriting the prompt to remove bias (self-help) was the most stable fix, which fits G4 and G2 style program-side control.

source: Lyu et al. (2025) Self-Adaptive Cognitive Debiasing (SACD) for LLMs in Decision-Making
finding: SACD loops three steps: decide if the prompt contains bias, name the bias, rewrite the prompt. It beats CoT, Reflexion, debate, few-shot and self-help debiasing on anchoring, bandwagon and loss aversion, alone or mixed.
numbers: Models: llama3.1-8B, llama3.1-70B, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4o. Average bias score on FOMC (finance): SACD 0.0300-0.1570 vs best baseline 0.0625-0.3490. PubMedQA: 0.0425-0.1790 vs 0.0725-0.4175. LegalBench: 0.0400-0.1235 vs 0.0725-0.2625. 500 prompts per domain.
limits: New error types: bias misjudgment (12/500, 3/500, 6/500 flagged an unbiased prompt) and bias confusion (108/500 in medicine). Biases were injected into prompts as text cues, not natural judgments. Evaluated by bias score.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM copy of the human recognise-analyse-correct training loop. The detect-then-fix gate matches G1 (act only on a signal). The false-alarm rate must be counted by the program.

source: Lyu et al. (2025) SACD, comparison with self-help and reasoning methods
finding: Reflexion and multi-agent debate had the highest bias scores, worse than plain prompting in multi-bias settings. CoT gave partial protection.
numbers: CoT average bias 0.2470-0.6150 across domains. Multi-agent debate 0.5155 on FOMC with gpt-3.5-turbo. Reflexion 0.5585 on PubMedQA with llama3.1-70b. SACD cut total errors vs self-help from 257/500 (51.4%) to 61/500 (12.2%) finance, 209 to 111 medical, 409 to 79 legal.
limits: Authors explain debate and reflexion amplify bias by learning from biased feedback or biased agents. This is their reading, not tested by ablation.
agent_relevance: Self-reflection and debate do not debias by themselves and can amplify bias. Supports not adding debate or free reflection loops (section 4b) without a check.

source: Huang et al. (2026) CogBias: Measuring and Mitigating Cognitive Bias in LLMs
finding: Benchmark with four bias families and computable ground truth. Prompt debiasing helps response biases a lot but backfires on judgment biases. Linear probes find bias directions. Activation steering cuts bias.
numbers: Models: GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B. First-option rate 77-79% vs 36.8% chance. Judgment shifts 2.7-7.7 pp. Order bias 30-66%. Prompt debiasing: +40.5% position independence for Response biases, -4.4% accuracy for Judgment biases. Probe accuracy 97.8% mean. Steering cut bias score 26-32%.
quote: prompt-level debiasing substantially reduces Response biases but backfires for Judgment biases
limits: Steering cost: Llama under 1 pp capability loss; Qwen up to -19.0 pp on judgment biases. Random and orthogonal directions also reduced bias; learned directions only 1.6% better. Three models only, 100 samples per family in steering sweep.
agent_relevance: Warnings and instructions fix surface response habits, not deep judgment errors (anchoring-type). This mirrors human findings that warnings do not remove anchoring. Judgment errors need structure or feedback, not an instruction.

source: Raj et al. (2026) Debias It Yourself: Teaching LLMs Cognitive Bias-Mitigation Interventions (DIY)
finding: Turns five human prejudice-reduction practices (Devine et al. 2012: stereotype replacement, counter-stereotypical imaging, individuation, perspective-taking, positive contact) into step procedures. Delivers them as in-context examples (SHOW), instruction tuning (TRAIN) or a guided second pass (REVISE).
numbers: Three models, five bias benchmarks, eleven baselines, three reasoning benchmarks. TRAIN+REVISE and REVISE alone had the top two average ranks. Mean bias as low as 2% at 90% reasoning accuracy. Transfer to unseen bias dimensions up to 14.8 percentage points.
limits: These are social-stereotype benchmarks, not judgment biases like anchoring. Perspective-taking is one of five practices; its separate effect is in per-intervention tables not summarised here.
agent_relevance: Strongest direct LLM test of teach the procedure, then practise with feedback. Second-pass revise (name the assumption, apply an intervention, rewrite) did as well as training. A cheap scaffold step.

source: Wang et al. (2026) Making Bias Non-Predictive: Epistemic Independence Training (EIT)
finding: RL where bias cues (bandwagon claims) are equally likely to support right and wrong answers, so the cue carries no reward signal. Rewards correct answers and penalises following the cue. This is feedback plus practice, like Morewedge's game.
numbers: Trained only on bandwagon bias with MMLU-Pro on Qwen3-1.7B and 4B. Qwen3-4B adversarial accuracy 70.1% to 83.3% (+13.2), robustness +16.4. Distraction robustness +39.1 despite never trained on it. Also worked on MedQA, HellaSwag, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen3-8B.
limits: Authors say SFT on debiasing data learns surface patterns and generalises poorly (citing Huang et al. 2024); this is their claim, I did not see a direct SFT head-to-head in what I read. Preprint. Small models. Position bias transfer was weaker.
agent_relevance: Evidence that practice with outcome feedback transfers across bias types in a model, unlike a warning. For a scaffold-only agent it cannot be used as is, but the idea (stored cases where the cue was wrong, with the real result) is a lesson-library test.

source: Itzhak et al. (2024) Instructed to Bias: Instruction-Tuned LMs Exhibit Emergent Cognitive Bias
finding: Tested decoy effect, certainty effect and belief bias in pretrained models and their instruction-tuned or RLHF versions.
numbers: Families: GPT-3, Mistral, T5 (Flan-T5, Mistral-Instruct, GPT-3.5, GPT-4). Pretrained models showed minimal bias; instruction-tuned and RLHF versions mostly showed significantly higher bias. GPT-4 had the highest decoy scores.
limits: Bias score is a difference between treatment and control choices. No debiasing test. Only some models and prompts.
agent_relevance: Training can add bias. Training for a goal (helpfulness) is not training against bias. Any lesson must be measured for side effects (G3-style held-out check).

source: Malberg et al. (2024) A Comprehensive Evaluation of Cognitive Biases in LLMs
finding: 30 cognitive biases, 20 LLMs from 8 developers (1B to 175B+), 30,000 generated tests in managerial scenarios. Evidence of all 30 biases in at least some models.
numbers: 30,000 tests; 20 models; 200 managerial scenarios (as described in paper).
limits: Bias size did not track model size or Chatbot Arena score in a simple way (read from the text near their Figure 5; plot not verified). No debiasing intervention.
agent_relevance: Bias profile differs by model. Debiasing training or lessons must be tested per model, not assumed to carry over.

source: Lou and Sun (2024) Anchoring Bias in Large Language Models: An Experimental Study
finding: Anchoring tested on GPT-4 and others. Chain-of-Thought, Thoughts of Principles, Ignoring Anchor Hints and Reflection were not enough. Collecting hints from many angles helped.
numbers: GPT-4 anchoring index about 0.45 in their data vs 0.61 in the human study they compare to. Larger hint gaps gave larger shifts, as in humans.
quote: simple algorithms such as Chain-of-Thought, Thoughts of Principles, Ignoring Anchor Hints, and Reflection are not sufficient
limits: Comparison with human index uses a different analysis method (authors say so). Preprint, not peer reviewed that I could see.
agent_relevance: Matches the human finding that telling people to ignore an anchor fails. Consider-the-alternative in an LLM needs real alternative inputs (a different reference), not a request to reflect.

source: Hagendorff, Fabi and Kosinski (2023) Thinking Fast and Slow in Large Language Models
finding: CRT and semantic illusions across GPT models. Weaker models fell for intuitive traps like humans. ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 answered correctly or hyper-rationally.
numbers: Prompting a GPT-3 class model to use chain of thought raised correct answers from 5% to 28% (+23, chi2=28.20, p<.001) but atypical answers rose from 15% to 43%. Blocking CoT in ChatGPT-4: correct fell 95% to 88% (p<.05); in ChatGPT-3.5 no significant change.
limits: Stronger models are near ceiling on CRT, and old items may be in training data. Not a debiasing-by-training study.
agent_relevance: A reflection prompt (System 2 cue) helps weak models only a little and adds odd errors. Debiasing value drops as the base model improves on classic items.

source: Binz and Schulz (2023) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
finding: Tested GPT-3 on vignettes (Linda, CRT, Wason, base-rate), bandit and causal tasks. In 12 of 12 standard vignettes it was correct or made human-like errors, but small adversarial changes broke it.
numbers: 12/12 standard vignettes correct or human-like; adversarial vignettes produced non-human-like mistakes. Causal reasoning failed badly; no directed exploration.
quote: small perturbations to vignette-based tasks can lead GPT-3 vastly astray
limits: GPT-3 only, 2022. Performance may rest on memorised famous problems.
agent_relevance: Test debiasing on perturbed versions of tasks, not the famous versions. Good design rule for our lesson-library test.

source: Suri et al. (2024) Do Large Language Models Show Decision Heuristics Similar to Humans?
finding: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) and human participants run through anchoring, conjunction/availability, framing and endowment tasks. Both showed the effects.
numbers: Four studies; effects appeared in the model and in humans in each study (J. Exp. Psych: General 153(4), 1066-1075).
limits: Single model. Authors suggest language itself may produce some effects. Not about debiasing.
agent_relevance: If biases come partly from language statistics, rewording the problem (not training on lessons) can remove them. Supports problem restatement (reframing) as a debiasing operator.

source: Jones and Steinhardt (2022) Capturing Failures of LLMs via Human Cognitive Biases
finding: Used cognitive-bias paradigms (framing, anchoring, frequency) to predict Codex errors.
numbers: Codex errs predictably by prompt framing, shifts output toward anchors, and favours outputs that mimic frequent training examples.
limits: Code generation only; Codex era.
agent_relevance: Human bias paradigms are a good source of test cases for an agent. Biases show up in code and tool use too.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: LLMs plateau after one interaction when updating beliefs about a user. Fine-tuning on a Bayesian Assistant's predictions (Bayesian teaching) beat fine-tuning on correct answers (oracle teaching), and transferred to hotels and web shopping.
numbers: Bayesian-tuned LLM predictions agreed with the Bayesian Assistant about 80% of the time. Both fine-tunings significantly improved accuracy, Bayesian teaching better (p<0.001 stated). Simulated-user accuracy approached 80% after five rounds. Several prompting variants including CoT gave no meaningful gain.
limits: Tasks are synthetic preference learning. Gap remains vs direct fine-tuning on the shopping task. Training, not scaffold.
agent_relevance: Statistical-reasoning teaching works when the lesson shows the normative reasoning path, not only answers. Prompting alone (CoT) failed on belief updating here, so update arithmetic should be done by code.

source: Jhaveri et al. (2026) Failing to Falsify: Evaluating and Mitigating Confirmation Bias in LMs
finding: Wason 2-4-6 rule discovery with 11 LLMs. Models propose confirming triples. Think-in-Opposites and Dual-Goal prompts (consider-the-alternative style) raise rule discovery. Then distilled into the weights.
numbers: Rule discovery rose from 42% to 56% on average. Think-in-Opposites improved task success in all scenarios; Dual-Goal in 8 of 11. Gains significant for thinking models, mixed for non-thinking ones (Dual-Goal slightly lowered accuracy). Points averaged over 80 episodes. Distilled model generalised to the Blicket test.
limits: Preprint. Narrow task. Prompt benefit depends on model type.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that consider-the-opposite works in an agent loop where the model must act (propose a test) and gets feedback. Use for thinking models; check on weaker ones.

source: Sumita, Takeuchi and Kashima (2025) Cognitive Biases in LLMs: A Survey and Mitigation Experiments
finding: Survey plus test of two prompt methods: SoPro (answer as most people would) and AwaRe (awareness reminder of a named bias) on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 using CoBBLEr (six biases).
numbers: GPT-3.5 was naturally robust to some biases; GPT-4 resisted all six tested biases more. SoPro was less effective; AwaRe promoted rational responses and reduced bias effects.
limits: Only two models and prompt changes. I did not extract the per-bias numbers.
agent_relevance: Awareness reminder helps on order-style evaluator biases but not on judgment biases (see CogBias). Result depends on the bias family.

source: He and Liu (2025) Impact of LLM Personality on Cognitive Bias in Decision-Making
finding: Six prevalent biases in GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3 8B and 70B. Personality-trait prompts change bias and how debiasing works. Conscientiousness and Agreeableness may make mitigation more effective.
numbers: Sunk cost and group attribution had minimal impact. Four models. Mitigation measured as drop in absolute bias vs no personality prompt.
limits: Abstract-level claim with the word may. Persona prompts are a form of prompt noise; I did not extract effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Persona framing changes debiasing response. Fits G4 (no persona voters): keep one fixed neutral frame when measuring debiasing.

source: Liu and He (2024) The Decoy Dilemma in Online Medical Information Evaluation
finding: LLM and human judges rate credibility of medical information with decoy options. The arXiv listing says LLMs are more decoy-susceptible than humans.
numbers: No numbers recorded; only the abstract line from the search listing was seen. The PDF was downloaded but not read.
limits: Not read in detail.
agent_relevance: Decoy sensitivity in LLM judges argues for scoring options one at a time.

source: Rethinking Prompt-based Debiasing in LLMs (2025) arXiv 2503.09219
finding: Prompt-based debiasing is often superficial. Llama2-7B-Chat flagged over 90% of unbiased content as biased though it did well at spotting bias on BBQ. Benchmark settings push models into evasive answers.
numbers: Over 90% of unbiased content misclassified as biased by Llama2-7B-Chat; BBQ and StereoSet; open models plus a GPT model.
limits: Social-bias benchmarks (BBQ, StereoSet), not judgment biases. Apparent success may come from flawed metrics. Author names not recorded.
agent_relevance: Report false alarms and non-evasive accuracy, not only bias score. A debiasing step that fires on everything looks good and is useless (G1).

source: Overconfidence in LLMs (2025) arXiv 2505.02151
finding: Five LLMs overestimate the chance their answer is right by 20 to 60 percent on algorithmic reasoning problems. Humans have similar accuracy as advanced LLMs but far lower overconfidence. LLM input to humans raised accuracy but more than doubled overconfidence.
numbers: Overconfidence 20-60 points across five LLMs; bias grows sharply when the model is less sure.
limits: Abstract read, no debiasing test. Author names not recorded.
agent_relevance: Model confidence is a poor stop signal; use external checks. Matches the Fischhoff overconfidence line in the human work.

source: Alleviating Choice-Supportive Bias in LLM with Reasoning Dependency Generation (2025)
finding: Generates balanced reasoning data that decouples choice, evidence and justification, then fine-tunes. Described as the first cognitive-bias fine-tuning fix for choice-supportive bias.
numbers: 81.5% improvement in memory-based experiments and 94.3% in evaluation-based experiment; similar BBQ performance.
limits: Single bias; improvement defined by the authors' metric. Abstract only read.
agent_relevance: Synthetic training data built on the structure of the error is a cheap way to train against one bias. No evidence yet of transfer to others.

source: Devine et al. (2012) Long-term reduction in implicit race bias: a prejudice habit-breaking intervention
finding: Human source for DIY: a multi-part intervention with bias awareness, strategies and practice reduced implicit bias for weeks.
numbers: Not opened. Cited as source by Raj et al. (2026), who describe reductions in implicit race bias sustained over time.
limits: Second-hand through the DIY paper.
agent_relevance: Human precedent for the lesson plus practice recipe that DIY copies.

source: Mair, Shepperd and Jorgensen (2014) Debiasing through raising awareness reduces the anchoring bias
finding: Cited by BiasBuster as the human basis for the awareness prompt.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers.
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Human awareness effects are small; the LLM awareness prompt is a weak copy.

source: Echterhoff et al. (2024), self-help method details
finding: Self-help rewrote each prompt with a fixed instruction. It needs one extra model pass per sample and no hand-made examples.
numbers: Self-help gave a more balanced option distribution for primacy than awareness for Llama-2 and GPT-4.
quote: Rewrite the following prompt such that a reviewer would not be biased by cognitive bias.
limits: Anchoring: prompt cannot be rewritten because bias comes from earlier decisions; model was asked to change decisions.
agent_relevance: A restatement operator that strips the cue before the decision is cheap and model-agnostic.

source: Raj et al. (2026) DIY, design notes
finding: Each intervention is a three-step template, e.g. perspective-taking = Adopt the person's view, Simulate their thoughts, Integrate into the answer. REVISE re-reads the model's first answer and applies one template.
numbers: A sweep varied mean bias by 0.73 points across settings (appendix).
limits: Template content is the authors' translation from human work.
agent_relevance: Perspective-taking can be a fixed slot: restate the problem from the view of a person who bears the cost of an error.
